ben: hey folks, first day snag. accepted the org invite but GitHub Desktop keeps failing pushes with a 403. the webview during SSO shows a banner complaining about third-party cookies and won't finish. who do I ping? cc @carol

carol: welcome ben! GitHub Desktop uses an embedded webview for oauth which sometimes gets blocked by SSO policies. can you paste the exact error from Desktop and whether you signed into Desktop as your work or personal account?

ben: Desktop error: 

"Authorization failed: SSO enforcement blocked. Please complete SSO to access org resources"

and the Desktop account dropdown shows I'm signed in as ben-personal. I thought I accepted the invite as ben.work. I tried "Sign in to GitHub.com" in Desktop and it opens a tiny window that says cookies blocked.

it-support: two things: 1) Desktop often auto-signed you in with your system default GH credentials (personal). 2) the embedded webview can be blocked by our SAML provider if third-party cookies or embedded flows are disabled. Workarounds: a) in Desktop, use "Sign in in browser" option (open in external browser) so SSO completes in your default browser; b) log out of your personal account in Desktop and add your work account; c) do `gh auth login` in terminal and Desktop will pick up credentials if it's using the gh CLI. Which OS are you on?

ben: macOS. I see a "Sign in in browser" button but when I click it nothing happens. The embedded window is the one showing the cookie banner.

devx: try holding option when clicking the sign-in button or check Desktop prefs -> Authentication to force external browser. Also check System Preferences -> Security & Privacy -> Privacy -> Cookies? On Mac Chrome/Safari you can allow cookies for the SSO provider domain. But easiest: run `gh auth login` in Terminal and choose web flow. After that in Desktop go to File -> Options -> Accounts and sign in using the work account.

ben: ran `gh auth login` and chose web flow, it opened my default browser, completed SSO and showed success. `gh auth status` shows I'm logged in as ben.work. In Desktop I still see ben-personal though.

it-support: quit Desktop fully and re-open. Desktop looks for local auth tokens on startup; restarting will pick up `gh` tokens. If it doesn't, go to Desktop -> Preferences -> Accounts and click "Sign in" then choose the work account; Desktop should now show ben.work. If Desktop still prefers personal, remove the personal account there first.

ben: restarted and signed in to ben.work in Desktop. tried to push and got a 403 once, then I cleared the local credential helper entries and retried and push succeeded. Thanks!

github-bot: Re-sent invite audit: user ben.work SSO enforcement = complete.

carol: great! follow-ups for onboarding doc: 1) note GitHub Desktop embedded webview issues and recommend `gh auth login` or "Sign in in browser"; 2) remind new hires to check which account Desktop is signed into (top-right avatar) before accepting invites. I'll add these as a short checklist.

it-support: closing thread  resolved. :white_check_mark:
